bss.topic: Meios de transporte: ontem e hoje

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um meio de transporte aéreo?
questions.hint: Aéreo tem a ver com o ar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um meio de transporte aquático?
questions.hint: Aquático tem a ver com a água.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um meio de transporte terrestre?
questions.hint: Terrestre anda sobre a terra.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chamam os transportes que andam sobre a terra, como o carro e o ônibus?
questions.hint: A palavra vem de "terra".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chamam os transportes que se movem na água, como o barco e o navio?
questions.hint: A palavra vem de "água".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O helicóptero é um transporte:
questions.hint: Onde o helicóptero se movimenta?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Antigamente, antes dos carros, muitas pessoas viajavam em:
questions.hint: Pense em transportes que usavam a força dos animais.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes transportes é mais moderno?
questions.hint: Qual deles usa trilhos e eletricidade nas grandes cidades?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Antes dos navios a motor, os barcos grandes eram movidos principalmente:
questions.hint: Pense no pano grande que fica no mastro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que puxava o bonde antes de ele ser elétrico?
questions.hint: Os primeiros bondes usavam a força de animais.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual transporte NÃO precisa de combustível nem de eletricidade para andar?
questions.hint: Qual deles anda com a força das pernas?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual grupo tem só transportes aquáticos?
questions.hint: Todos precisam estar na água.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Uma viagem que hoje leva poucas horas de avião levava, no passado, muitos dias de navio. Isso mostra que os transportes ficaram:
questions.hint: Compare o tempo da viagem antes e agora.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes é um transporte coletivo, que leva muitas pessoas ao mesmo tempo?
questions.hint: Coletivo quer dizer para muita gente junta.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Cite uma vantagem e uma desvantagem dos carros em relação às carroças de antigamente.
questions.hint: Pense na velocidade e também na poluição ou no trânsito.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual meio de transporte você usa para ir à escola? Ele é terrestre, aquático ou aéreo? Explique.
questions.hint: Pense no caminho que ele faz: na terra, na água ou no ar.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What are inverted commas used for?
options: To show the words someone says
questions.answer: To show the words someone says
questions.hint: They are also called speech marks.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is another name for inverted commas?
questions.hint: They mark speech.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses inverted commas correctly?
options: "Let's go to the park," said Mia.
"Let's go to the park, said Mia."
Let's go "to the park," said Mia.
questions.answer: "Let's go to the park," said Mia.
questions.hint: Only the spoken words go inside.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In the sentence: "I love pizza," said Leo. Which words are spoken?
questions.hint: Look inside the inverted commas.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In the sentence: "Where is my hat?" asked Grandpa. Who is the speaker?
questions.hint: Look at the words outside the inverted commas.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Where does the comma go? "It is raining___" said Ruby.
options: Inside the inverted commas, after raining
questions.answer: Inside the inverted commas, after raining
questions.hint: The punctuation stays with the spoken words.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.hint: Tom is asking a question. Where should the question mark go?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What should you do when a new person starts speaking in a story?
questions.hint: This helps the reader see who is talking.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: The spoken words always start with a:
questions.hint: Look at the first letter after the opening inverted commas.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word could replace 'said' to show someone is speaking very quietly?
questions.hint: Think of a soft, quiet voice.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: How many people are speaking? "Hello," said Zara. "Hi!" replied Omar.
questions.hint: Count the speakers' names.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which punctuation mark is missing at the end of the spoken words? "Is it lunchtime___" asked Ben.
questions.hint: Ben wants to know something.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence has the inverted commas in the wrong place?
options: "My dog" is called Rex, said Ana.
"My dog is called Rex," said Ana.
Ana said, "My dog is called Rex."
questions.answer: "My dog" is called Rex, said Ana.
questions.hint: Check that all the spoken words are inside.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite this with the correct punctuation: we are late said Mum
questions.hint: Find the spoken words first, then add inverted commas, a capital letter and a comma.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write two lines of dialogue between two friends at the beach. Use inverted commas and start a new line for each speaker.
questions.hint: Each friend gets their own line.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does it mean to infer?
options: To work something out from clues in the text
To copy words from the text
questions.answer: To work something out from clues in the text
questions.hint: Think about being a reading detective.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a quotation?
options: The exact words copied from the text
questions.answer: The exact words copied from the text
questions.hint: You use inverted commas around it.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do we use a quotation when we answer a question?
options: To prove our answer with evidence
questions.answer: To prove our answer with evidence
questions.hint: Think about how a detective proves an idea.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Kai slammed the door and stomped up the stairs.' How does Kai feel?
questions.hint: Look at the verbs 'slammed' and 'stomped'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Lily's hands shook as she stepped onto the stage.' How does Lily feel?
questions.hint: What makes hands shake before a show?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'The giant robot stared at the empty plate and its eyes dimmed.' What does the robot probably want?
questions.hint: The plate is empty.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Rosa hid the broken vase behind the sofa.' Why did Rosa hide the vase?
options: She did not want anyone to know she broke it
She wanted to fix it later in the garden
She thought it was a present
questions.answer: She did not want anyone to know she broke it
questions.hint: Why do people hide things?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Sam wrapped his scarf tighter and watched his breath make clouds.' What is the weather like? (one word)
questions.hint: When can you see your breath?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'The farmer looked at the giant footprints in his field and ran to the village.' Which quotation shows the farmer was worried?
questions.hint: Which action shows he wanted help quickly?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A motive is:
options: the reason why a character does something
the place where a story happens
the last part of a story
questions.answer: the reason why a character does something
questions.hint: Think about 'why' questions.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Ben gave his last biscuit to the little boy who was crying.' What can we infer about Ben?
questions.hint: What does his action show?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'The metal man sat alone on the cliff, looking at the town lights below.' How might the metal man feel?
questions.hint: Look at the word 'alone'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which is the best way to start an answer that uses evidence?
options: I think this because the text says...
questions.answer: I think this because the text says...
questions.hint: You need your idea and your proof.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Mo's mouth watered when he smelled the bread from the bakery.' What does Mo want? (one or two words)
questions.hint: What did he smell?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Ella kept looking at the clock and tapping her foot.' How does Ella feel? Use a quotation to prove it.
questions.hint: Pick the words that give you a clue, and put them in inverted commas.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'The robot lifted the trapped sheep gently out of the hole.' What does this tell us about the robot? Explain with evidence.
questions.hint: Think about the word 'gently'.
